title: Staged release API & SDK: health hooks, shadowing, and rollback primitives
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Design and ship an API + SDK ergonomics for staged model releases that unifies canary schedules, A/B traffic splitting, shadow traffic toggles, and automated rollback triggers. The API must be safe for production: idempotent, auditable, and enforceable by RBAC scopes.

Scope:
- New REST endpoints to create/update/delete a staged release manifest (weight schedules, shadow rules, health triggers).
- SDK client helpers (Python/TS) for declarative manifests and transactional apply semantics.
- Idempotency token semantics for CLI/SDK calls to prevent double-apply on retry.
- Fine-grained permission scopes: rollout.create, rollout.modify, rollout.rollback, rollout.shadow.
- Auto-rollback primitives driven by health hooks (latency p95, error-rate, quality regression signals) and pluggable alert sources.
- Audit logging and immutable changelog entries for compliance.
- Backward-compatible behavior for existing rollout routes.

API contract (high level):
- POST /v1/rollouts: create a staged-release resource with optional idempotency_token header. Body includes targets (model:version), schedule (steps with duration + weight), shadow_rules (percentage, routes), health_checks (metrics, threshold, window), and rollback_policy (immediate/cooldown/escalate).
- PATCH /v1/rollouts/:id/apply-step to manually advance/cancel a step (requires rollout.modify).
- POST /v1/rollouts/:id/rollback to trigger manual rollback (requires rollout.rollback).
- GET /v1/rollouts/:id/history returns immutable changelog and audit entries.
- POST /v1/rollouts/simulate for dry-run that returns estimated traffic distribution and expected safety checks.

SDK helpers:
- Context manager style API in Python: with rollouts.staged_release(manifest) as r: r.apply() -> returns operation handle with progress() and wait(timeout).
- Idempotent apply using client-side generated idempotency tokens; SDK reuses token across retries and surface partial-apply state for callers.
- Helper to attach health-hook listeners that can be wired to Redwood Console metrics or external monitoring webhooks.

Idempotency and concurrency model:
- Clients pass Idempotency-Token header on create/modify operations. Server ensures exactly-once semantics for token within 72h window.
- Concurrent patch semantics use optimistic locking with rollout.etag returned in GET; PATCH requires matching etag or explicit force flag (force requires higher permission scope).

Permissions and audit:
- New RBAC scopes defined and added to Console role mappings.
- Audit events emitted for create/modify/step-advance/rollback with actor, token, and diff.
- Sensitive fields (e.g., rollback to model versions with restricted access) require both rollout.modify and model.promote scope.

Safety & auto-rollback behaviour:
- Health checks evaluate metrics over sliding windows and can mark a step as unhealthy when thresholds breach for >2 consecutive windows.
- On unhealthy step, system can either pause rollout and alert, or automatically revert traffic back to previous stable version based on rollout.rollback_policy.
- Auto-rollback can be configured to be 'immediate' (roll back to last stable), 'gradual' (reduce weight back to zero over N minutes), or 'escalate' (pause + page on-call + wait for manual).

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit tests for idempotency handling and etag concurrency.
- Integration tests against staging Console metrics pipeline to simulate p95 spikes and error rate regressions.
- End-to-end test that creates a rollout, advances steps, injects metric regression, and asserts auto-rollback and audit log entries.
- Feature flag gated behind rollout-api-v2 until we validate across customers.

Artifacts / Specs:
- Design doc: https://docs.redwood.internal/rollouts/staged-release-api (prototype spec and sequence diagrams)
- API proto: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollouts/blob/main/api/v1/rollouts.proto
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/12345

Acceptance criteria:
- API endpoints implemented and passing unit + integration tests in CI.
- SDK wrappers for Python + TypeScript published to internal package index and sample usage in quickstarts.
- RBAC scopes wired into Console roles and audit logs show a complete changelog for a sample rollout.
- Auto-rollback triggered in staging test harness and logs show correct revert sequence.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Should idempotency tokens be scoped to org or global? (Current plan: org-scoped to avoid cross-org collisions.)
- How long to retain idempotency token history (72h current default vs 7d for increased safety)?
- Should we support multi-model rollouts (fan-out) in v1 or postpone to v2? (Plan: v1 single model target, v2 multi-target)

Migration notes:
- Existing rollout endpoints remain functional; new staged-release resource will coexist. Migration guide to map existing canary manifests to staged-release manifest will be published in Console docs.
